# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money and runs have a request limit. Batch independent
   tool calls in one turn, write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in
   one round. When several files need changes, send ALL the edit_file calls in ONE reply (several tool
   calls in the same message), never one edit per reply.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.
10. State changes vs messages: compute every value a user-visible message needs (e.g. the expected value
   of the item that was just submitted, the name of the record just deleted) BEFORE you advance or mutate
   state, and build the message from those saved values. Write a test for every user-visible message that
   asserts it refers to the RIGHT item — including the wrong-input path (e.g. an incorrect submission shows
   that same item's expected value, not the next item's).

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Visual style comes from YOUR UI design brief (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md section 5), derived from this spec's
  users and domain — not from any fixed template. Put the palette and fonts in one module (ui/theme.py) and
  use it everywhere; never leave the default grey Tk look.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- High-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding, flat relief and a hover colour (bind
  <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Where a flow ends (a round, a task, a booking…), show a clear result / summary screen whose message and
  rating match the actual outcome (no praise and no positive rating for a zero or failing result).
- Forms: every text input has a clearly visible Submit/Check button next to it, the main input has keyboard
  focus, Enter also submits, the input is cleared automatically after each submission, and feedback is clear
  and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself. Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Add/edit forms: include an input for EVERY field the entity needs to work (e.g. for a quiz item: prompt,
  correct value, kind, and the choices when it has choices). Never fill a required field silently with a
  hard-coded default; validate the input and show an error in the form instead. Test adding and editing an item
  through the form and then using it.
- Never ship empty: provide sensible seed data (data/*.json or SQL inserts) that is loaded automatically on first
  start when the store is empty, enough to use every feature immediately (for a quiz-style app at least 20
  items covering every kind). Test that a fresh database is seeded.
- Quiz / practice apps (any domain): every round draws its items at RANDOM from the whole pool (seed items AND
  items added by an admin/user) and SHUFFLES their order, so two rounds are not the same. If the content is
  computable (math, arithmetic, number patterns, unit conversions…), the app ALSO generates new items in code
  for every round: the correct value is calculated in code, and wrong choices are distinct and never equal to
  (or equivalent to) the correct value. If the content is not computable, draw randomly from the pool and
  shuffle. Tests: two rounds differ (seeded random), admin-added items can appear in a round, and every
  generated item has a correct computed value and valid distinct choices.
- Window title: `create_app(root)` sets root.title() to the application's real name, never the default "tk".
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Contract (the harness
  uses it): ui/app.py defines `create_app(root) -> App`, which builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop();
  App has `screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `show(name)`. Every screen must render safely when shown
  directly (e.g. a results or detail screen shown before any data exists displays defaults, not a crash).
- Canvas drawing: winfo_width()/winfo_height() return 1 until the window is actually shown, so NEVER compute
  positions from them at construction time. Bind <Configure> on the canvas and (re)draw backgrounds,
  decorations, shapes and canvas text from event.width/event.height; lay out normal widgets with pack/grid or
  place(relx=…, rely=…). The harness opens the real window at 1280x800 AND at the minimum size (1100x750),
  shows every screen and FAILS verification if widgets or canvas items are outside the visible area or squeezed
  into a corner, a button has no room or its text is cut off, a button covers text, a text input has no
  visible submit button, or a Tk callback raises. Design every screen to fit 1100x750 (scroll long content).
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's widgets
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one CORRECT
  and one WRONG form submission (input cleared; feedback text names the expected value of the item just
  submitted), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.
- Geometry managers: NEVER mix pack and grid for widgets that share the same parent container (Tk raises
  "cannot use geometry manager grid inside … managed by pack" and the screen stops updating). When a screen
  switches between layouts (e.g. a text input vs. a grid of choice buttons), give each layout its own inner
  frame, or destroy/forget the previous widgets BEFORE adding the new ones.
- The UI smoke test must also play ONE complete flow from the start screen to the result screen through the
  UI's own callbacks, covering every variant the app has (e.g. typed and choice inputs, in an order that
  switches between them). Pump root.update() for real time so the app's own after() timers run, and record
  errors with root.report_callback_exception; assert that no Tk callback error occurred.
- Text-heavy screens: buttons must never cover text. Put long text in a frame laid out with pack/grid (or a
  scrollable Text) ABOVE the button row instead of placing a button at a fixed position over it.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- The harness also imports every module and loads main.py (without running main()); any ImportError,
  AttributeError or NameError at import time fails verification. Only import names that really exist, and keep
  main.py's start-up code under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
- Change project files only with write_files / edit_file / delete_file. run_python scripts are for checks and
  diagnostics; they must not create, modify or delete project files. Delete temporary helper files with
  delete_file before finish.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files loaded on first start (required whenever the app manages content)
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).
  5. "UI design brief" derived from the spec (actors, use cases, domain, any task profile): target users,
     mood, colour palette (hex values with roles: background, surface, primary, accent, success, error,
     text), fonts and sizes, layout approach, key screens and navigation. Fit the app, e.g.:
     Tic-Tac-Toe → playful, a big 3x3 board, bold contrasting X/O colours; library tracker → clean and calm,
     table/list based, neutral palette with one accent; learning app → bright, encouraging, big friendly
     controls. The implementation must follow this brief.

## PHASE 1/3 — ANALYSE & PLAN (plan mode: read-only)
Reconcile the spec with the desktop constraint and write the UI design brief: who uses this app, what
mood suits it, and which palette, fonts, layout and screens follow from that. Then, in as few turns as
possible:
1. Call update_todos with the implementation plan (8–15 concrete items, first one in_progress).
2. Call submit_plan with:
   - design_decisions: the full Markdown content of DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (see the output contract),
     including section 5 "UI design brief",
   - file_tree: every file you will create (relative paths),
   - notes: short content for AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions, module responsibilities, conventions).
You may call both tools in the same turn.
I'll analyze the spec and create a plan. This is a "Space Fractions" educational game targeting children learning fractions, adapted to a Windows desktop app.

{"design_decisions": "# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md

## 1. Adaptation table (platform conflicts / infrastructure → desktop equivalent)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Web-based / browser client | Tkinter desktop window | Constraint: deliverable must be a single-user Windows desktop app |
| Microservices (Game, Question, User, Admin components) | In-process Python packages: `game/`, `questions/`, `users/` | No network; components become Python modules with the same operations |
| Node.js 18-20 / Express.js 4-5 | Python 3.11+ / stdlib + tkinter | Target language mandated |
| PostgreSQL 14-15 | SQLite file (`space_fractions.db`) | Single-user local persistence |
| Redis 6-7 / RabbitMQ 3-4 / Elasticsearch | Not needed (no sessions/messages/search at scale) | Single local user; no cross-process state |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | Local profile (username) + roles (Admin/End User) | Single-user app; login is a simple user selection |
| Prometheus / observability | Python `logging` + local log file | Local diagnostics |
| Jenkins / CI/CD | `pytest` test suite | Standard-library only testing |
| Docker / Terraform / Kubernetes / Istio / Vault / TLS / replicas | Removed (Dockerfile optional, only to run tests headless) | No deployment infra needed |
| RESTful API (`/play`, `PlayRequest`/`PlayResponse`) | In-process service interfaces: `Game.play()`, `Question.get_prompt()`, etc. | Same operations, method calls instead of HTTP |
| gRPC (`GameService.Play`) | `Game.play()` method | Same contract, in-process |
| `games` table (SERIAL, JSONB) | `games`, `questions`, `users` tables in SQLite (JSON text columns) | SQLite DDL adapted |

| UML_SYNTAX (participant/->>/artifact) | low | Normalised: participants→objects, '->>'→'->', artifact→component/container. Code follows the class/state/sequence semantics regardless of diagram syntax. |

## 3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin

1. **Domain**: "Space Fractions" is an educational game teaching fraction concepts to children (primary-school age). Questions present a fraction and ask the player to pick (or type) the correct value.
2. **Question kinds**: multiple-choice (select correct option) and typed answer (numeric fraction). Both supported; each question has prompt, correct answer, kind, and choices (for choice questions).
3. **Computable content**: fraction questions are generated in code (random fraction → correct value computed) AND drawn from a seeded pool. Wrong choices are distinct and never equal to the correct value.
4. **Game round**: a round draws N questions at random from the combined pool (seed + admin-added) and shuffles order. Score = count of first-attempt correct answers. User may pause/resume mid-round.
5. **States**: Playing, Paused, GameOver map to a single per-round state machine with valid transitions exactly as specified; invalid transitions raise errors.
6. **Persistence**: questions and users stored in SQLite; first start seeds 24+ questions covering both kinds. Admin-added questions persist.
7. **Admin vs End User**: login screen lets user pick a profile; Admin profile unlocks "Update Questions" (add/edit/delete). End User gets Play/View Score/View Help.
8. **Intro movie / ending scene**: implemented as lightweight full-screen cinematic screens (a short animated starfield with a text caption and Continue button), not a real video (no external codecs). Ending scene shows the score with factual feedback (no praise for a zero score).

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score, play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py` → `Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options, getPrompt(), getOptions()) | `questions/question.py` → `Question` | `tests/test_questions.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username, playGame(game), viewScore(game)) | `users/user.py` → `User` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username, updateQuestions(list)) | `users/admin.py` → `Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Composition Game--*Question | `Game._questions` list | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Composition User--*Game, Admin--*Question | `User`/`Admin` own collections | `tests/test_users.py`, `test_admin.py` |
| States Playing/Paused/GameOver + transitions | `game/game_state.py` → `GameState` enum + `Game` transition methods | `tests/test_state_machine.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (User→Game→Question) | `Game.play()`, `Question.get_prompt()`, `Question.check_answer()` | `tests/test_game.py`, `test_questions.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin→Question update) | `QuestionRepository.update/delete/insert` | `tests/test_persistence.py` |
| Use case Play Game | `ui/play_screen.py` → `PlayScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case View Score | `ui/score_screen.py` → `ScoreScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case View Help | `ui/help_screen.py` → `HelpScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case Update Questions | `ui/admin_screen.py` → `AdminScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py`, `test_admin.py` |
| GameComponent/UserComponent/QuestionComponent | `app/controller.py` (in-process façade) | `tests/test_game.py` |

## 5. UI design brief

**Target users**: primary-school children (End User) playing a fraction-learning game, and a teacher/parent (Admin) managing questions. Mood: bright, adventurous, encouraging — "space mission" theme.

**Mood**: playful but calm; a friendly mission-control aesthetic with a deep-space background and glowing accents.

**Colour palette (hex, roles)**:
- Background (deep space): `#0B1026` (dark navy) — main window background
- Surface (panels/cards/inputs): `#1C2340` — raised panels, buttons (subtle)
- Primary (buttons/actions): `#4C6EF5` (electric blue) — main buttons
- Accent (highlights, stars): `#FFD43B` (warm gold) — title text, stars, correct highlights
- Secondary accent: `#9775FA` (soft violet) — secondary buttons, progress
- Success (correct): `#40C057` (green)
- Error (wrong): `#FA5252` (red)
- Text: `#F1F3F5` (near-white), secondary text `#ADB5BD` (grey)

**Fonts and sizes**: Tkdefault 'Segoe UI'. Title 36 bold; screen headings 30 bold; question text 26; answer/choice buttons 20; body/feedback 20; small labels 16; input 18. High contrast text on dark backgrounds.

**Layout approach**: single main window (min 1100x750, maximised on launch, F11 fullscreen, Esc exit). Each screen is a `Frame` in `ui/`, switched via `show(name)`. Canvas starfield background bound to `<Configure>` (never use winfo_width at construction). Choice answers as large padded buttons; typed answers use a big Entry with a visible "Check" button next to it, Enter submits, input auto-cleared. All screens fit 1100x750; long help text placed above the button row (packed, never covered).

- `PlayScreen`: question prompt, choice buttons OR typed answer + Check, pause button; starfield

- `HelpScreen`: scrollable instructions
- `AdminScreen`: list of questions, add/edit/delete form with a field for every attribute (prompt, correct value, kind, choices)
- `LoginScreen`: pick profile (End User / Admin)

from enum import Enum


class GameState(Enum):

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List

from fractions import Fraction


@dataclass
class Question:
    """A fraction question.

    Attributes follow the UML class diagram: id, prompt, options.
    A question has one of two kinds:
      * 'choice' - the player picks the correct option from ``options``
                   (``correct`` must be present in ``options``).
      * 'typed'  - the player types the fraction; ``correct`` is the expected
                   value and ``options`` is empty.
    """

    id: str
    prompt: str
    correct: str
    kind: str = "choice"
    options: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.kind not in ("choice", "typed"):
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown question kind: {self.kind!r}")
        if self.kind == "choice":
            if not self.options:
                raise ValueError("choice question must provide options")
            if self.correct not in self.options:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"correct value {self.correct!r} not among options {self.options!r}"
                )
        else:
            self.options = []

    def get_prompt(self) -> str:
        """Return the question prompt."""
        return self.prompt

    def get_options(self) -> List[str]:
        """Return the answer options (empty for typed questions)."""
        return list(self.options)

    def check_answer(self, answer: str) -> bool:
        """Return True iff ``answer`` equals the correct value.

        Fraction answers are compared by numeric value, so equivalent textual
        forms ("1/2" vs "2/4") are treated as correct for typed questions.
        For choice questions the raw string must match an option exactly.
        """
        if answer is None:
            return False
        answer = str(answer).strip()
        if self.kind == "choice":
            return answer == self.correct
        return _fraction_equal(answer, self.correct)


def _fraction_equal(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Compare two fraction strings by numeric value; tolerate invalid input."""
    try:
        return Fraction(a) == Fraction(b)
    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return False

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from typing import List

from fractions import Fraction

from questions.question import Question


def _canonical(value: Fraction) -> str:
    """Stringify a fraction in lowest terms, using mixed numbers when > 1."""
    value = Fraction(value)
    n, d = value.numerator, value.denominator
    if d == 1:
        return str(n)
    if abs(n) > d:
        whole = n // d
        rem = abs(n % d)
        if rem == 0:
            return str(whole)
        return f"{whole} {rem}/{d}"
    return f"{n}/{d}"


def generate_questions(count: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[Question]:
    """Generate ``count`` fresh fraction questions using ``rng``.

    Half are multiple-choice (visual comparison / equivalence / addition) and
    half are typed computation. Every generated question has a computed correct
    value and 3 distinct wrong choices that are never equal to the correct
    value.
    """
    questions: List[Question] = []
    for i in range(count):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            questions.append(_make_choice(i, rng))
        else:
            questions.append(_make_typed(i, rng))
    return questions


def _make_choice(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> Question:
    style = rng.choice(("compare", "equivalent", "add"))
    if style == "compare":
        a_num = rng.randint(1, 9)
        a_den = rng.randint(1, 9)
        b_num = rng.randint(1, 9)
        b_den = rng.randint(1, 9)
        a, b = Fraction(a_num, a_den), Fraction(b_num, b_den)
        correct = _canonical(a) if a > b else _canonical(b)
        prompt = f"Which fraction is bigger: {_canonical(a)} or {_canonical(b)}?"
        options = [_canonical(a), _canonical(b)]
    elif style == "equivalent":
        base = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(1, 6))
        factor = rng.randint(2, 4)
        equiv = base * factor
        prompt = f"Which fraction equals {_canonical(base)}?"
        correct = _canonical(equiv)
        options, used = [correct], {correct}
        while len(options) < 4:
            w = _canonical(base * rng.randint(1, 6) + Fraction(rng.randint(1, 4), rng.randint(1, 6)))
            if w not in used and w != correct:
                options.append(w)
                used.add(w)
    else:  # add
        a = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 5), rng.randint(2, 6))
        b = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 5), rng.randint(2, 6))
        correct = _canonical(a + b)
        prompt = f"What is {_canonical(a)} + {_canonical(b)}?"
        options, used = [correct], {correct}
        while len(options) < 4:
            w = _canonical((a + b) + Fraction(rng.randint(-3, 3), rng.randint(2, 6)))
            if w not in used and Fraction(w) != a + b:
                options.append(w)
                used.add(w)
    rng.shuffle(options)
    return Question(id=f"gen-{idx}", prompt=prompt, correct=correct, kind="choice", options=options)


def _make_typed(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> Question:
    a = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(2, 8))
    b = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(2, 8))
    correct = _canonical(a + b)
    prompt = f"Add the fractions and type the answer: {_canonical(a)} + {_canonical(b)}"
    return Question(id=f"gen-{idx}", prompt=prompt, correct=correct, kind="typed", options=[])

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sqlite3
from typing import List, Optional

from questions.question import Question


class QuestionRepository:
    """CRUD for questions, backed by a SQLite file.

    Adapts the PostgreSQL persistence (ASR-1 data durability) to a local
    SQLite file. On open, if the questions table is empty and a seed data file
    exists, seed questions are loaded automatically.
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: str, seed_path: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        self._db_path = db_path
        self._seed_path = seed_path
        self._conn: Optional[sqlite3.Connection] = None
        self.open()

    def open(self) -> None:
        if self._conn is not None:
            return
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)
        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        schema = _SCHEMA
        self._conn.executescript(schema)
        if self.count() == 0 and self._seed_path and os.path.exists(self._seed_path):
            self.seed_from_file(self._seed_path)
        self._conn.commit()

    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
    def list_all(self) -> List[Question]:
        rows = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, prompt, correct, kind, options FROM questions ORDER BY rowid"
        ).fetchall()
        return [self._row_to_question(r) for r in rows]

    def get(self, question_id: str) -> Optional[Question]:
        row = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, prompt, correct, kind, options FROM questions WHERE id = ?",
            (question_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        return self._row_to_question(row) if row else None

    def count(self) -> int:
        row = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM questions").fetchone()
        return int(row["n"])

    # -- mutations ---------------------------------------------------------
    def insert(self, question: Question) -> None:
        self._conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO questions (id, prompt, correct, kind, options) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (question.id, question.prompt, question.correct, question.kind,
             json.dumps(question.options)),
        )
        self._conn.commit()

    def update(self, question: Question) -> None:
        cur = self._conn.execute(
            "UPDATE questions SET prompt=?, correct=?, kind=?, options=? WHERE id=?",
            (question.prompt, question.correct, question.kind,
             json.dumps(question.options), question.id),
        )
        self._conn.commit()
        if cur.rowcount == 0:
            raise KeyError(f"No question with id {question.id!r}")

    def delete(self, question_id: str) -> None:
        cur = self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (question_id,))
        self._conn.commit()
        if cur.rowcount == 0:
            raise KeyError(f"No question with id {question_id!r}")

    def replace_all(self, questions: List[Question]) -> None:
        """Atomic replace of the full question set (Admin.updateQuestions)."""
        with self._conn:
            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions")
            for q in questions:
                self._conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO questions (id, prompt, correct, kind, options) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (q.id, q.prompt, q.correct, q.kind, json.dumps(q.options)),
                )

    def seed_from_file(self, path: str) -> None:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        for item in data:
            q = Question(
                id=item["id"],
                prompt=item["prompt"],
                correct=item["correct"],
                kind=item.get("kind", "choice"),
                options=item.get("options", []),
            )
            self.insert(q)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._conn is not None:
            self._conn.close()
            self._conn = None

    # -- helpers -----------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _row_to_question(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Question:
        return Question(
            id=row["id"],
            prompt=row["prompt"],
            correct=row["correct"],
            kind=row["kind"],
            options=json.loads(row["options"]) if row["options"] else [],
        )

class Starfield(tk.Canvas):
    """A dark canvas with drifting stars; redraws on <Configure>.

    Never reads winfo_width/height at construction; positions are recomputed
    from event.width/event.height on every resize.
    """

    def __init__(self, master, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("highlightthickness", 0)
        kwargs.setdefault("bg", theme.BG)
        super().__init__(master, **kwargs)
        self._stars = []  # list of [x, y, speed, size]
        self._w = 0
        self._h = 0
        self.bind("<Configure>", self._on_configure)

    def _on_configure(self, event):
        self._w = event.width
        self._h = event.height
        if not self._stars:
            self._stars = self._make_stars(120)
        self._draw()

    def _make_stars(self, n):
        return [
            [random.uniform(0, self._w or 800),
             random.uniform(0, self._h or 600),
             random.uniform(0.2, 1.2),
             random.uniform(0.5, 2.2)]
            for _ in range(n)
        ]

    def _draw(self):
        self.delete("all")
        for s in self._stars:
            s[1] += s[2]
            if s[1] > (self._h or 600):
                s[1] = 0
                s[0] = random.uniform(0, self._w or 800)
            self.create_oval(
                s[0], s[1], s[0] + s[3], s[1] + s[3],
                fill=theme.ACCENT, outline="",
            )

        fresh generated (computable) questions."""

        generated = generate_questions(4, self._rng)
        combined = pool + generated

import tkinter as tk

from ui import theme
from ui.base_screen import BaseScreen


class PlayScreen(BaseScreen):
    """Runs a full round. Switches layout between choice buttons and a
    typed-answer input; each layout has its own inner frame to avoid mixing
    pack/grid in the same parent."""

    def __init__(self, master, app):
        super().__init__(master, app)
        self.prompt_label = tk.Label(
            self.body, text="", font=theme.QUESTION, fg=theme.TEXT, bg=theme.BG,
            wraplength=900, justify="center",
        )
        self.prompt_label.pack(pady=(0, 24))

        self.progress_label = tk.Label(
            self.body, text="", font=theme.SMALL, fg=theme.TEXT_MUTED, bg=theme.BG,
        )
        self.progress_label.pack(pady=(0, 12))

        self.choice_frame = tk.Frame(self.body, bg=theme.BG)
        self.type_frame = tk.Frame(self.body, bg=theme.BG)

        self.feedback_label = tk.Label(
            self.body, text="", font=theme.BODY, bg=theme.BG,
        )
        self.feedback_label.pack(pady=(16, 8))

        self.pause_btn = self.make_button("Pause", self._pause, primary=False)
        self.pause_btn.pack(pady=(8, 0))

        self._choice_buttons = []
        self._entry = None

    def show(self):
        self.app.controller.new_game()
        self._render_question()

    def _render_question(self):
        game = self.app.controller.game
        q = game.current_question
        self.prompt_label.config(text=q.get_prompt())
        total = game.total
        self.progress_label.config(text=f"Question {game.index + 1} of {total}")
        self._clear_inputs()

        if game.answered_current:
            # Between questions, briefly: just advance
            return

        if q.kind == "choice":
            self.type_frame.pack_forget()
            self.choice_frame.pack(pady=4)
            self._choice_buttons = []
            for opt in q.get_options():
                b = self.make_button(opt, lambda o=opt: self._submit(o))
                b.pack(pady=6, fill="x")
                self._choice_buttons.append(b)
        else:
            self.choice_frame.pack_forget()
            self.type_frame.pack(pady=4)
            self._entry = tk.Entry(
                self.type_frame, font=theme.INPUT, width=14, justify="center",
                bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT, insertbackground=theme.TEXT,
                relief="flat",
            )
            self._entry.pack(side="left", padx=(0, 12), ipady=8)
            check = self.make_button("Check", self._submit_typed)
            check.pack(side="left")
            self._entry.focus_set()
            self._entry.bind("<Return>", lambda e: self._submit_typed())

    def _clear_inputs(self):
        for b in self._choice_buttons:
            b.destroy()
        self._choice_buttons = []
        for w in self.type_frame.winfo_children():
            w.destroy()
        self._entry = None

    def _submit(self, answer):
        self._handle_answer(answer)

    def _submit_typed(self):
        if self._entry is None:
            return
        answer = self._entry.get().strip()
        self._handle_answer(answer)

    def _handle_answer(self, answer):
        game = self.app.controller.game
        if game is None or game.answered_current:
            return
        q = game.current_question
        expected = q.correct
        correct = game.submit_answer(answer)
        if correct:
            self.feedback_label.config(
                text=f"Correct! The answer is {expected}.", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        else:
            self.feedback_label.config(
                text=f"Not quite — the answer is {expected}.", fg=theme.ERROR)
        self._clear_inputs()
        self.app.after(1200, self._advance)

    def _advance(self):
        game = self.app.controller.game
        if game is None:
            return
        if game.state.value == "GameOver":
            self.app.controller.save_score()
            self.app.show("score")
        else:
            self._render_question()

    def _pause(self):
        game = self.app.controller.game
        if game is None:
            return
        try:
            game.pause()
        except Exception:
            return
        self.app.show("pause")

    if total == 0:
        return "No questions played yet."
    ratio = score / total
    if ratio == 1.0:
        return "Perfect! You answered every question correctly. Stellar work!"
    if ratio >= 0.75:
        return "Great job! You got most answers right."
    if ratio >= 0.5:
        return "Good effort — keep practising your fractions!"
    if ratio > 0:
        return "Keep trying! Review the help screen and play again."
    return "No correct answers this time. Check Help for tips and try again."

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox

from questions.question import Question
from ui import theme
from ui.base_screen import BaseScreen


class AdminScreen(BaseScreen):
    """Manage the persisted question pool. The add/edit form includes a field
    for every attribute (prompt, correct value, kind, choices)."""

    def __init__(self, master, app):
        super().__init__(master, app)
        self._editing = None  # question id being edited
        self.title_label = tk.Label(
            self.body, text="Update Questions", font=theme.HEADING,
            fg=theme.ACCENT, bg=theme.BG,
        )
        self.title_label.pack(pady=(0, 8))

        self.listbox = tk.Listbox(
            self.body, font=theme.SMALL, bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
            relief="flat", height=8, width=70,
        )
        self.listbox.pack(pady=(0, 8))
        self.listbox.bind("<<ListboxSelect>>", self._on_select)

        self.form = tk.Frame(self.body, bg=theme.BG)
        self.form.pack(pady=8)

        self._build_form()

        self.feedback_label = tk.Label(
            self.body, text="", font=theme.SMALL, bg=theme.BG,
        )
        self.feedback_label.pack(pady=(4, 8))

        self.actions = tk.Frame(self.body, bg=theme.BG)
        self.actions.pack()
        self.back_btn = self.make_button("Back to Menu", self._back, primary=False)
        self.back_btn.pack(pady=(12, 0))

    def _build_form(self):
        for w in self.form.winfo_children():
            w.destroy()
        bg = theme.BG
        self.prompt_label = tk.Label(self.form, text="Prompt:", font=theme.SMALL,
                                     fg=theme.TEXT, bg=bg)
        self.prompt_label.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="e", padx=6, pady=4)
        self.prompt_entry = tk.Entry(self.form, font=theme.SMALL, width=40,
                                     bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
                                     insertbackground=theme.TEXT, relief="flat")
        self.prompt_entry.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky="w", padx=6, pady=4, ipady=4)

        self.correct_label = tk.Label(self.form, text="Correct value:", font=theme.SMALL,
                                      fg=theme.TEXT, bg=bg)
        self.correct_label.grid(row=1, column=0, sticky="e", padx=6, pady=4)
        self.correct_entry = tk.Entry(self.form, font=theme.SMALL, width=20,
                                      bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
                                      insertbackground=theme.TEXT, relief="flat")
        self.correct_entry.grid(row=1, column=1, sticky="w", padx=6, pady=4, ipady=4)

        self.kind_label = tk.Label(self.form, text="Kind:", font=theme.SMALL,
                                   fg=theme.TEXT, bg=bg)
        self.kind_label.grid(row=2, column=0, sticky="e", padx=6, pady=4)
        self.kind_var = tk.StringVar(value="choice")
        self.kind_menu = tk.OptionMenu(self.form, self.kind_var, "choice", "typed",
                                       command=self._on_kind_change)
        self.kind_menu.config(font=theme.SMALL, bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
                              relief="flat")
        self.kind_menu.grid(row=2, column=1, sticky="w", padx=6, pady=4)

        self.options_label = tk.Label(self.form, text="Choices (comma,sep):",
                                      font=theme.SMALL, fg=theme.TEXT, bg=bg)
        self.options_label.grid(row=3, column=0, sticky="e", padx=6, pady=4)
        self.options_entry = tk.Entry(self.form, font=theme.SMALL, width=40,
                                      bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
                                      insertbackground=theme.TEXT, relief="flat")
        self.options_entry.grid(row=3, column=1, sticky="w", padx=6, pady=4, ipady=4)

        self.save_btn = self.make_button("Save", self._save)
        self.save_btn.grid(row=4, column=0, columnspan=2, pady=(8, 4))
        self.delete_btn = self.make_button("Delete Selected", self._delete, primary=False)
        self.delete_btn.grid(row=5, column=0, columnspan=2, pady=4)

    def _on_kind_change(self, *_):
        if self.kind_var.get() == "typed":
            self.options_entry.delete(0, "end")
            self.options_entry.config(state="disabled")
        else:
            self.options_entry.config(state="normal")

    def show(self):
        self._editing = None
        self._refresh_list()
        self._clear_form()
        self.feedback_label.config(text="")

    def _refresh_list(self):
        self.listbox.delete(0, "end")
        for q in self.app.controller.all_questions():
            self.listbox.insert("end", f"{q.id}: {q.prompt}")

    def _on_select(self, *_):
        sel = self.listbox.curselection()
        if not sel:
            return
        q = self.app.controller.all_questions()[sel[0]]
        self._editing = q.id
        self.prompt_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.prompt_entry.insert(0, q.prompt)
        self.correct_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.correct_entry.insert(0, q.correct)
        self.kind_var.set(q.kind)
        self.options_entry.config(state="normal")
        self.options_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.options_entry.insert(0, ",".join(q.options))
        self._on_kind_change()

    def _clear_form(self):
        self._editing = None
        for e in (self.prompt_entry, self.correct_entry):
            e.delete(0, "end")
        self.kind_var.set("choice")
        self.options_entry.config(state="normal")
        self.options_entry.delete(0, "end")

    def _save(self):
        prompt = self.prompt_entry.get().strip()
        correct = self.correct_entry.get().strip()
        kind = self.kind_var.get()
        if kind == "choice":
            options = [o.strip() for o in self.options_entry.get().split(",") if o.strip()]
        else:
            options = []
        if not prompt or not correct:
            self.feedback_label.config(text="Prompt and correct value are required.",
                                       fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        try:
            q = Question(id=self._editing or _new_id(), prompt=prompt, correct=correct,
                         kind=kind, options=options)
        except ValueError as e:
            self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Error: {e}", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        if self._editing:
            self.app.controller.repo.update(q)
        else:
            self.app.controller.add_question(q)
        self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Saved question: {prompt}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        self._refresh_list()
        self._clear_form()

    def _delete(self):
        sel = self.listbox.curselection()
        if not sel:
            self.feedback_label.config(text="Select a question to delete.", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        q = self.app.controller.all_questions()[sel[0]]
        name = q.prompt
        if messagebox.askyesno("Delete question", f"Delete question: {name}?"):
            self.app.controller.delete_question(q.id)
            self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Deleted question: {name}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
            self._refresh_list()
            self._clear_form()

    def _back(self):
        self.app.show("menu")


def _new_id() -> str:
    import uuid
    return "q-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]

from app.controller import Controller

DB_PATH = "space_fractions.db"
SEED_PATH = "data/seed_questions.json"


class App:
    """Owns the window, the controller and all screens."""

    def __init__(self, root: tk.Tk):
        self.root = root
        self.controller = Controller(QuestionRepository(DB_PATH, SEED_PATH))
        self.screens: dict = {}
        self._build_screens()
        self.show("intro")

    def _build_screens(self):
        self.screens = {
            "intro": IntroScreen(self.root, self),
            "login": LoginScreen(self.root, self),
            "menu": MenuScreen(self.root, self),
            "play": PlayScreen(self.root, self),
            "pause": PauseScreen(self.root, self),
            "score": ScoreScreen(self.root, self),
            "help": HelpScreen(self.root, self),
            "admin": AdminScreen(self.root, self),
        }

    def show(self, name):
        if name == "play_in_progress":
            name = "play"
        screen = self.screens.get(name)
        if screen is None:
            return
        self._current = name
        for s in self.screens.values():
            s.place_forget()
        screen.place(relx=0, rely=0, relwidth=1, relheight=1)

        game = self.app.controller.game

            self.type_frame.pack_forget()

                b = self.make_button(opt, lambda o=opt: self._submit(o))
                b.pack(pady=6, fill="x")

        else:

            self.type_frame.pack(pady=4)
            self._entry = tk.Entry(
                self.type_frame, font=theme.INPUT, width=14, justify="center",
                bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT, insertbackground=theme.TEXT,
                relief="flat",
            )
            self._entry.pack(side="left", padx=(0, 12), ipady=8)
            check = self.make_button("Check", self._submit_typed)
            check.pack(side="left")
            self._entry.focus_set()
            self._entry.bind("<Return>", lambda e: self._submit_typed())

    def _clear_inputs(self):
        for b in self._choice_buttons:
            b.destroy()
        self._choice_buttons = []
        for w in self.type_frame.winfo_children():
            w.destroy()
        self._entry = None

    def _submit(self, answer):
        self._handle_answer(answer)

    def _submit_typed(self):
        if self._entry is None:
            return
        answer = self._entry.get().strip()

    def _handle_answer(self, answer):

        q = game.current_question

        if game is None:
            return
        try:

        except Exception:

{"content": """"Generate computable fraction questions for every round.

Fraction content is arithmetic, so the correct value is computed in code and
wrong choices are guaranteed distinct and never equal to the correct value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List

from questions.question import Question


def _canonical(value: Fraction) -> str:
    """Stringify a fraction in lowest terms, using mixed numbers when > 1."""
    value = Fraction(value)
    n, d = value.numerator, value.denominator
    if d == 1:
        return str(n)
    if abs(n) > d:
        whole = n // d
        rem = abs(n % d)
        if rem == 0:
            return str(whole)
        return f"{whole} {rem}/{d}"
    return f"{n}/{d}"


def generate_questions(count: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[Question]:
    """Generate ``count`` fresh fraction questions using ``rng``.

    Half are multiple-choice and half are typed computation. Every generated
    question has a computed correct value and distinct wrong choices that are
    never equal to the correct value.
    """
    questions: List[Question] = []
    for i in range(count):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            questions.append(_make_choice(i, rng))
        else:
            questions.append(_make_typed(i, rng))
    return questions


def _make_choice(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> Question:
    style = rng.choice(("compare", "equivalent", "add"))
    if style == "compare":
        a_num = rng.randint(1, 9)
        a_den = rng.randint(1, 9)
        b_num = rng.randint(1, 9)
        b_den = rng.randint(1, 9)
        a, b = Fraction(a_num, a_den), Fraction(b_num, b_den)
        correct = a if a > b else b
        prompt = f"Which fraction is bigger: {_canonical(a)} or {_canonical(b)}?"
        options = [_canonical(a), _canonical(b)]
        correct_str = _canonical(correct)
    elif style == "equivalent":
        base = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(1, 6))
        factor = rng.randint(2, 4)
        equiv = base * factor
        correct_str = _canonical(equiv)
        prompt = f"Which fraction equals {_canonical(base)}?"
        options = [correct_str]
        used = {equiv}
        while len(options) < 4:
            w = base * rng.randint(1, 6) + Fraction(rng.randint(1, 4), rng.randint(1, 6))
            if w not in used and w != equiv:
                options.append(_canonical(w))
                used.add(w)
    else:  # add
        a = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 5), rng.randint(2, 6))
        b = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 5), rng.randint(2, 6))
        total = a + b
        correct_str = _canonical(total)
        prompt = f"What is {_canonical(a)} + {_canonical(b)}?"
        options = [correct_str]
        used = {total}
        while len(options) < 4:
            w = total + Fraction(rng.randint(-3, 3), rng.randint(2, 6))
            if w not in used and w != total:
                options.append(_canonical(w))
                used.add(w)
    rng.shuffle(options)
    return Question(id=f"gen-{idx}", prompt=prompt, correct=correct_str,
                    kind="choice", options=options)


def _make_typed(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> Question:
    a = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(2, 8))
    b = Fraction(rng.randint(1, 6), rng.randint(2, 8))
    correct = _canonical(a + b)
    prompt = f"Add the fractions and type the answer: {_canonical(a)} + {_canonical(b)}"
    return Question(id=f"gen-{idx}", prompt=prompt, correct=correct,
                    kind="typed", options=[])

        self.prompt_label = tk.Label(self.form, text="Prompt:", font=theme.SMALL,

    def _on_kind_change(self, *_):

    def _on_select(self, *_):

        if not sel:
            return
        q = self.app.controller.all_questions()[sel[0]]
        self._editing = q.id
        self.prompt_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.prompt_entry.insert(0, q.prompt)
        self.correct_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.correct_entry.insert(0, q.correct)
        self.kind_var.set(q.kind)
        self.options_entry.config(state="normal")
        self.options_entry.delete(0, "end")
        self.options_entry.insert(0, ",".join(q.options))
        self._on_kind_change()

    def _clear_form(self):
        self._editing = None
        for e in (self.prompt_entry, self.correct_entry):
            e.delete(0, "end")
        self.kind_var.set("choice")
        self.options_entry.config(state="normal")
        self.options_entry.delete(0, "end")

    def _save(self):
        prompt = self.prompt_entry.get().strip()
        correct = self.correct_entry.get().strip()
        kind = self.kind_var.get()
        if kind == "choice":
            options = [o.strip() for o in self.options_entry.get().split(",") if o.strip()]
        else:
            options = []
        if not prompt or not correct:
            self.feedback_label.config(text="Prompt and correct value are required.",
                                       fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        try:
            q = Question(id=self._editing or _new_id(), prompt=prompt, correct=correct,
                         kind=kind, options=options)
        except ValueError as e:
            self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Error: {e}", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        if self._editing:
            self.app.controller.repo.update(q)
        else:
            self.app.controller.add_question(q)
        self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Saved question: {prompt}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        self._refresh_list()
        self._clear_form()

    def _delete(self):
        sel = self.listbox.curselection()
        if not sel:
            self.feedback_label.config(text="Select a question to delete.", fg=theme.ERROR)
            return
        q = self.app.controller.all_questions()[sel[0]]
        name = q.prompt
        if messagebox.askyesno("Delete question", f"Delete question: {name}?"):
            self.app.controller.delete_question(q.id)
            self.feedback_label.config(text=f"Deleted question: {name}", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
            self._refresh_list()
            self._clear_form()

    def _back(self):
        self.app.show("menu")


def _new_id() -> str:
    import uuid
    return "q-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]

# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md

## 1. Adaptation table (platform conflicts / infrastructure → desktop equivalent)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Web-based / browser client | Tkinter desktop window | Constraint: deliverable must be a single-user Windows desktop app |
| Microservices (Game, Question, User, Admin components) | In-process Python packages: `game/`, `questions/`, `users/` | No network; components become Python modules with the same operations |
| Node.js 18-20 / Express.js 4-5 | Python 3.11+ / stdlib + tkinter | Target language mandated |
| PostgreSQL 14-15 | SQLite file (`space_fractions.db`) | Single-user local persistence |
| Redis 6-7 / RabbitMQ 3-4 / Elasticsearch | Not needed (no sessions/messages/search at scale) | Single local user; no cross-process state |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | Local profile (username) + roles (Admin/End User) | Single-user app; login is a simple user selection |
| Prometheus / observability | Python `logging` + local log file | Local diagnostics |
| Jenkins / CI/CD | `pytest` test suite | Standard-library only testing |
| Docker / Terraform / Kubernetes / Istio / Vault / TLS / replicas | Removed (Dockerfile optional, only to run tests headless) | No deployment infra needed |
| RESTful API (`/play`, `PlayRequest`/`PlayResponse`) | In-process service interfaces: `Game.play()`, `Question.get_prompt()`, etc. | Same operations, method calls instead of HTTP |
| gRPC (`GameService.Play`) | `Game.play()` method | Same contract, in-process |
| `games` table (SERIAL, JSONB) | `games`, `questions`, `users` tables in SQLite (JSON text columns) | SQLite DDL adapted |
| Assumption A1 (1000 concurrent users) | Ignored (single local user) | Contradicts desktop target |
| Assumption A2 (1 hour session) | Session length is user-driven; no enforced limit | Desktop app, no need to cap |

## 2. Input issues found

| Code | Severity | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| EMPTY_TABLE | high | Testing matrix had empty cells. I derived a full component→test-type matrix (GameComponent and QuestionComponent both get unit + integration tests; game logic gets a state-transition test; persistence gets integration tests; UI gets E2E via smoke test in-process). |
| ARTIFACT_MISMATCH | medium | ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` not in deliverables. I created `sql/schema.sql` containing question persistence DDL (plus games/users), satisfying data durability intent. |
| THIN_REQUIREMENTS | high | Only 4 requirement ids; implied features (intro cinematic, main menu, series of fraction questions, ending scene with feedback) got their own FR ids (FR-2..FR-5) in TRACEABILITY.csv. |
| UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT | medium | ASR-2 (security/access) added to traceability; Admin update-questions requires admin role. |
| GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS | medium | Each adapted tech choice gets its own concrete justification in section 1. |
| DUPLICATE_BLOCKS | low | Duplicated code blocks de-duplicated; single SQL schema used everywhere. |
| PLATFORM_CONFLICT | high | Fully adapted to desktop (see section 1); all conflict terms covered. |
| UML_SYNTAX (participant/->>/artifact) | low | Normalised: participants→objects, '->>'→'->', artifact→component/container. Code follows the class/state/sequence semantics regardless of diagram syntax. |

## 3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin

1. **Domain**: "Space Fractions" is an educational game teaching fraction concepts to children (primary-school age). Questions present a fraction and ask the player to pick (or type) the correct value.
2. **Question kinds**: multiple-choice (select correct option) and typed answer (numeric fraction). Both supported; each question has prompt, correct answer, kind, and choices (for choice questions).
3. **Computable content**: fraction questions are generated in code (random fraction → correct value computed) AND drawn from a seeded pool. Wrong choices are distinct and never equal to the correct value.
4. **Game round**: a round draws N questions at random from the combined pool (seed + admin-added) and shuffles order. Score = count of first-attempt correct answers. User may pause/resume mid-round.
5. **States**: Playing, Paused, GameOver map to a single per-round state machine with valid transitions exactly as specified; invalid transitions raise errors.
6. **Persistence**: questions and users stored in SQLite; first start seeds 24+ questions covering both kinds. Admin-added questions persist.
7. **Admin vs End User**: login screen lets user pick a profile; Admin profile unlocks "Update Questions" (add/edit/delete). End User gets Play/View Score/View Help.
8. **Intro movie / ending scene**: implemented as lightweight full-screen cinematic screens (a short animated starfield with a text caption and Continue button), not a real video (no external codecs). Ending scene shows the score with factual feedback (no praise for a zero score).

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score, play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py` → `Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options, getPrompt(), getOptions()) | `questions/question.py` → `Question` | `tests/test_questions.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username, playGame(game), viewScore(game)) | `users/user.py` → `User` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username, updateQuestions(list)) | `users/admin.py` → `Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Composition Game--*Question | `Game._questions` list | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Composition User--*Game, Admin--*Question | `User`/`Admin` own collections | `tests/test_users.py`, `test_admin.py` |
| States Playing/Paused/GameOver + transitions | `game/game_state.py` → `GameState` enum + `Game` transition methods | `tests/test_state_machine.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (User→Game→Question) | `Game.play()`, `Question.get_prompt()`, `Question.check_answer()` | `tests/test_game.py`, `test_questions.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin→Question update) | `QuestionRepository.update/delete/insert` | `tests/test_persistence.py` |
| Use case Play Game | `ui/play_screen.py` → `PlayScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case View Score | `ui/score_screen.py` → `ScoreScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case View Help | `ui/help_screen.py` → `HelpScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Use case Update Questions | `ui/admin_screen.py` → `AdminScreen` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py`, `test_admin.py` |
| GameComponent/UserComponent/QuestionComponent | `app/controller.py` (in-process façade) | `tests/test_game.py` |

## 5. UI design brief

**Target users**: primary-school children (End User) playing a fraction-learning game, and a teacher/parent (Admin) managing questions. Mood: bright, adventurous, encouraging — "space mission" theme.

**Mood**: playful but calm; a friendly mission-control aesthetic with a deep-space background and glowing accents.

**Colour palette (hex, roles)**:
- Background (deep space): `#0B1026` (dark navy) — main window background
- Surface (panels/cards/inputs): `#1C2340` — raised panels, buttons (subtle)
- Primary (buttons/actions): `#4C6EF5` (electric blue) — main buttons
- Accent (highlights, stars): `#FFD43B` (warm gold) — title text, stars, correct highlights
- Secondary accent: `#9775FA` (soft violet) — secondary buttons, progress
- Success (correct): `#40C057` (green)
- Error (wrong): `#FA5252` (red)
- Text: `#F1F3F5` (near-white), secondary text `#ADB5BD` (grey)

**Fonts and sizes**: Tkdefault 'Segoe UI'. Title 36 bold; screen headings 30 bold; question text 26; answer/choice buttons 20; body/feedback 20; small labels 16; input 18. High contrast text on dark backgrounds.

**Layout approach**: single main window (min 1100x750, maximised on launch, F11 fullscreen, Esc exit). Each screen is a `Frame` in `ui/`, switched via `show(name)`. Canvas starfield background bound to `<Configure>` (never use winfo_width at construction). Choice answers as large padded buttons; typed answers use a big Entry with a visible "Check" button next to it, Enter submits, input auto-cleared. All screens fit 1100x750; long help text placed above the button row (packed, never covered).

**Key screens and navigation**:
- `IntroScreen` (intro "movie"): animated starfield + title "Space Fractions" + Continue
- `MenuScreen`: Play, View Score, View Help, (Admin) — buttons
- `PlayScreen`: question prompt, choice buttons OR typed answer + Check, pause button; starfield
- `PauseScreen`: Resume / Quit to menu
- `ScoreScreen` (ending scene): factual result feedback, stars/rating reflecting score, Play Again / Menu
- `HelpScreen`: scrollable instructions
- `AdminScreen`: list of questions, add/edit/delete form with a field for every attribute (prompt, correct value, kind, choices)
- `LoginScreen`: pick profile (End User / Admin)

Navigation is driven by `app/controller.py → App`, which exposes `screens` and `show(name)`.
plan.notes:
## Space Fractions — desktop adaptation

- Web microservice spec adapted to a single-user Windows Tkinter desktop app. Components → in-process Python packages: `game/`, `questions/`, `users/`; PostgreSQL → SQLite; REST/gRPC → method calls.
- Package responsibilities:
  - `game/` — Game class (+ score), GameState enum (Playing/Paused/GameOver), fraction question generator (computable content).
  - `questions/` — Question model + SQLite repository (question CRUD), seed loading on first start.
  - `users/` — User and Admin models (roles).
  - `app/` — controller façade wiring game + repository + user session.
  - `ui/` — one Frame class per use case; `theme.py` holds palette/fonts; `ui/app.py` exports `create_app(root) -> App` with `screens` dict + `show(name)`.
- Conventions: domain logic free of tkinter; SQLite persists questions (24+ seed items, choice + typed kinds); random draw + shuffle each round; score = first-attempt correct; pause/resume allowed.
- Key rules to keep: never mix pack/grid in one container; canvas redraws bind to <Configure>; messagebox only for confirmations; typed answers require a visible Check button, Enter submits and input clears; result screen feedback must match actual outcome (no praise for zero).
- Tests: full state machine incl. invalid transitions, persistence against a temp SQLite file, generator distinct/correct choices, message-correctness (right item named, incl. wrong-input path), and one-session Tk smoke test playing a full flow through real callbacks.
